transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my eating has gotten really out of hand. Most nights, after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen eating way more than a normal meal. Like fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls—whatever leftovers are there. Sometimes it feels like I go through a whole tray or half the fridge before I stop.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yeah. Once I take that first bite, it feels like I’ve already lost control. I’ll be telling myself, “George, stop, that’s enough,” but I just keep making another plate or opening another container anyway.
Do these episodes of eating happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that. Sometimes I’m upset or tense, but other times it just happens at night and I don’t really know what set it off.
Do these episodes of eating ever happen during the day, or is it always at night?
I’m not really sure. I notice it most at night, after things quiet down, but I can’t say for sure it never happens during the day. I just haven’t paid close enough attention to that.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these late-night eating episodes?

Yeah. Pretty much every time afterward, I feel sick with myself. I’ll be sitting there thinking, I’m supposed to be this organized, strong person, and here I am ashamed and guilty and disgusted that I let it happen again.
How often do these episodes of eating happen?
For months now, I honestly can’t think of a week where it didn’t happen at least once. Most weeks it’s more than that — several nights, usually after my wife goes to bed.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these episodes?

Yeah, I do. I eat really fast when it’s happening. Sometimes I barely even taste the food, even stuff I normally care about making. I’ll be standing at the counter taking big bites and swallowing before I’ve really finished chewing the last one.
Have you ever had one of these eating episodes where you didn't feel guilty or ashamed afterward?
Honestly, no. I can’t really think of a time where I felt okay afterward. It’s pretty much always this sick feeling with myself — ashamed, guilty, disgusted that I let it happen again.
Have you ever had one of these episodes of eating like this during the day?
I’m not really sure. I mostly think of it happening at night, so I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s happened during the day too.
Do you usually try to hide or conceal the evidence of your late-night eating from your wife or others?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m hiding things afterward. I know I feel bad about it, but I don’t know if I’m specifically trying to cover it up.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of my weight, so I can’t say if it’s changed a lot recently.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes?
I’m not sure. I guess a lot of the time it’s when no one else is around, but I haven’t really kept track of whether I’m always alone when it happens.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Yeah. Most nights after my wife goes to bed, I’ll end up in the kitchen and eat way more than a normal meal. Like fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls… and if there are leftovers from something, I’ll keep going until a whole tray or a lot of what’s in the fridge is gone. It can happen pretty fast, within a couple hours.
Do you think these episodes of eating ever happen during the day?
I’m not really sure. I notice it more at night, but I can’t say for certain it never happens during the day.
Do you ever feel a sense of pleasure or euphoria while you're eating during these episodes?
I don’t know if I’d call it pleasure or euphoria. I’m usually just focused on eating in the moment. I haven’t really paid attention to feeling “good” exactly.
Do you usually feel hungry before one of these eating episodes happens?

A lot of the time, no. I might have already eaten dinner with my wife, and then later I still go back to the kitchen and start picking at leftovers. It just turns into eating a whole lot again, even though I wasn’t really hungry to begin with.
Do you usually think about food or look forward to eating before one of these episodes happens?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’m usually looking forward to it in some planned way. Sometimes food is just there, or I end up thinking about it, but I haven’t really noticed a clear build-up beforehand.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started during these episodes?

Yes. Once I start, it feels like I’ve already lost the choice. I’ll be telling myself, “George, stop now,” but I’m still getting another plate or opening something else. It’s like my hands just keep going even though part of me knows I should stop.
